paragraphs.text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome-4 (CDLS4) is a cohesinopathy characterized by growth retardation, minor skeletal anomalies, and facial features that overlap those of Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS). Cognitive impairment is much milder than in patients with classical CdLS caused by mutation in NIPBL, SMC1A, or SMC3 (Deardorff et al., 2012). Overall, affected individuals have an attenuated CdLS phenotype. Facial dysmorphism, limb anomalies, and cognitive and behavioral involvement are all less marked, and there is striking interfamilial and intrafamilial variability (Krab et al., 2020). Some patients have holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics (Kruszka et al., 2019; Krab et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Compared with NIPBL and SMC1A cohorts, the patients reported by Krab et al. (2020) had an attenuated CdLS phenotype. Common facial features included: - long and/or smooth philtrum (90%) - short nose (88%) - concave nasal ridge (83%) - thick eyebrows (83%) - long eyelashes (81%) - thin upper lip vermilion (79%) - upturned nasal tip (70%) - synophrys (68%) - arched eyebrows (67%) Other findings were: - short fifth finger (82%) - postnatal head circumference below -2 SD (57%) - clinodactyly of the fifth finger (54%) - gastroesophageal reflux (52%) - dislocated elbow or abnormal elbow extension (46%) - ptosis (42%) - heart anomalies (39%) - hirsutism (38%) - postnatal height below -2 SD (37%) - hearing loss (33%) - cleft or submucous cleft palate (24%) - seizures (9%) No patient had a major limb malformation or visual impairment. Hands and feet were generally of normal size. Growth at birth was generally less impaired than in the other cohorts, and short stature and microcephaly developed postnatally. Unusual anomalies included vertebral anomalies (clefts and hemivertebrae) and relatively frequent malformations of structures derived from the embryonic foregut. Diaphragmatic hernia, anal atresia, and choanal atresia occurred occasionally.

paragraphs.text: Cognitive function in the cohort reported by Krab et al. (2020) was normal in 3 of 29 patients and mildly impaired in 13 of 29. Four patients had moderate disability, and none had severe or profound disability. All patients aged 3 years and above used some words. Development showed more language-based than motor-based problems. Fourteen of 25 patients had behavioral problems, mainly anxiety, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, and obsessive-compulsive behavior. Aggression and self-injurious behavior were each found in only 1 patient. Some affected individuals had children of their own and were diagnosed only after a more severely affected child was recognized. Additional phenotypes seen in individuals with limited clinical information (cohort B) included holoprosencephaly, with or without CdLS characteristics.

paragraphs.text: Krab et al. (2020) reported 31 different RAD21 alterations in 33 families: 7 unique deletions and 24 intragenic sequence variants. Two variants were recurrent: C585R and R586X were each found in 2 families. Of the 24 sequence variants, 13 were predicted to be truncating: 2 nonsense, 2 splice site, and 9 frameshift variants, scattered throughout the gene. Three were in-frame deletions, and the missense variants tended to cluster in the functional domains of the protein. Krab et al. (2020) used protein modeling and molecular dynamics to study 12 variants. They concluded that at least 6 were likely pathogenic: S345P, P376R, C585R, R586Q, Q592del, and L603P. In a family with Mungan syndrome, affected individuals carried biallelic A622T variants, and heterozygous family members had some features of the CdLS spectrum. Whether this variant causes a phenotype in the heterozygous state remained uncertain.

paragraphs.text: In a 15-month-old boy with CDLS4, Gudmundsson et al. (2019) used exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous 3-bp deletion (c.1774_1776del) in the RAD21 gene, resulting in deletion of gln592 (Gln592del). The boy had developmental delay, CdLS-like facial features, reflux, testis retention, prominent digit pads, and diaphragmatic hernia. In silico structural modeling predicted that the deletion breaks the contacts between RAD21 lys591 and SMC1A glu1191 and glu1192. Molecular dynamics analysis by Krab et al. (2020) showed that the deletion displaces lys605 and thereby affects the positioning of SMC1A asn35 at ATPase site 1.
